General Dynamics revealed a new artificial intelligence-enabled, portable communications system on Thursday called the Vion, a Mission Partner Environment solution. Although its basic purpose is to give ground troops a suitcase-sized platform to exchange messages and files, the company said its real value is how it connects allied systems.
In an interview with Military Times, Jason Myers, vice president of defense agencies at General Dynamics Information Technology, explained that Vion can help ground troops quickly establish secure connections with a command center and coalition forces from remote environments.
Using open architecture and AI, he said Vion will connect with outside networks, adapt to or patch connections and translate written messages, voice memos, videos and more, all while maintaining zero-trust cybersecurity protections .
“We wanted to provide an all-encompassing offering, but we didn’t want to lock somebody into an offering or not be able to use where they’ve already invested,” Myers said.
He added that most organizations want a custom communications kit, and most companies aim to provide platforms that only work with proprietary equipment and software. But those things can make it challenging and expensive to update or upgrade systems.
“What we wanted to do is say, ‘Yes, we’re going to use proven technologies,’ but as new things come out, we are absolutely ripping and replacing those, and how to do that securely, in that modular architecture, is really, really different than how things are being done today,” he said.
According to the company, GDIT participated in a Joint Staff J6-led demonstration called Olympus Fires, where the Defense Information Systems Agency , or DISA, explored ways to improve the Coalition Information Environment , or CIE, which it described as “a modernized architecture built on the principles of Zero Trust and data centricity.”
At a panel discussion in June, U.S. Army Lt. Col. David Courter, DISA’s Combatant Command Integration and Plans chief, explained the goal of the event was to “broker and federate our environments together without replicating a new environment every time.”
Explaining the need for the CIE solutions, Jason Martin, DISA’s Component Acquisition Executive, referenced a friendly fire incident in March , in which Kuwaiti air defenses mistakenly shot down three U.S. F-15E Strike Eagle fighter jets.
“We’ve spent the past 50 years building siloed networks, siloed applications and siloed environments to collaborate internally with our own data. We can no longer do that,” Martin said. “We have to converge networks. We have to plug and play. We have to talk to one another … We have to operate and maintain command and control with a single voice.”
Myers said GDIT is currently working through the acquisitions process for Vion but declined to say with whom. However, he said he thinks Vion, in terms of service, will “have a very long life in where it can add value to the mission.”

Posted By: Henry Lazenby October 29, 2026
Apollo Silver (TSXV: APGO; US-OTC: APGOF) estimates initial capital of $633 million (C$888.3 million) for its Calico project in California, which could produce about 5 million oz. silver annually over 15 years.
A preliminary economic assessment released Thursday puts after-tax net present value at $737 million using a 5% discount rate, with a 25% internal rate of return at $55-per-oz. silver. The proposed open-pit operation would mine the Waterloo deposit, about 15 km northeast of Barstow in San Bernardino County.
“Our focus now is de-risking: studies on water, power and capital inputs are under way, and we are advancing toward a prefeasibility study,” CEO Colin Sutherland said in the release.
The assessment gives Apollo a development blueprint for a silver mine in the United States, with engineering, financing and permitting work still ahead. The economics rely on silver revenue alone, leaving the nearby Langtry deposit and Waterloo’s gold resource outside the mine plan.
Apollo shares fell 11% to C$1.70 by Thursday afternoon in Toronto, valuing the company at about C$107 million.
Price sensitivity
The study, prepared by SLR Consulting, proposes contract mining and an 8,000-tonne-per-day processing plant producing doré on site. It estimates total recovered silver production of 74.4 million oz., with all-in sustaining costs averaging $26.07 per payable ounce.
Higher-grade material would be processed first, averaging about 101 grams silver per tonne over the first decade. Some lower-grade material would be stockpiled for later treatment, with processing continuing through year 15.
Initial capital includes a 25% contingency, with total capital over the project’s life estimated at $715 million after sustaining spending, pit backfilling and closure costs. The study assumes two years of construction and an after-tax payback of three years from production startup. Capital estimates carry an accuracy range of 30% below to 50% above the stated figures.
Returns are sensitive to silver prices. At $45 per oz., after-tax net present value falls to $348 million and the internal rate of return drops to 16%. At $65 silver, those figures rise to $1.11 billion and 32%, respectively.
Recovery tests
The processing plan assumes 65% silver recovery, supported by laboratory testing on five Waterloo samples. Finer grinding improved recoveries, making that stage of the proposed plant important to achieving the study’s assumptions.
Apollo plans further testing to assess recovery across different types of mineralization and refine processing. The plant design includes filtered, dry-stack tailings to recycle most process water.
Water rights would need to be acquired or leased within the Mojave Basin. Apollo must also confirm a power connection, including available capacity on nearby transmission lines.
Although Waterloo and Langtry lie on private land with county-recognized vested surface mining rights, Apollo hasn’t obtained the permits needed to construct or operate the project.
The company expects permitting to proceed mainly under California environmental and reclamation laws, with San Bernardino County as lead agency. Federal environmental review could also apply if a project component requires a federal permit or federal funding is used. Environmental baseline studies are planned for next year.
Resource revision
An updated estimate effective Oct. 1 puts Waterloo’s resource at 42.2 million measured and indicated tonnes grading 85.1 grams silver per tonne for 115.6 million ounces. Another 1.1 million inferred tonnes grading 65.4 grams contain 2.3 million ounces.
Langtry holds 23 million inferred tonnes grading 66.3 grams silver for 49.1 million oz., excluded from the proposed operation.
Waterloo’s measured and indicated silver inventory declined 7.5% from 125 million oz. in the June 2025 estimate , while tonnage decreased 23% and average grade increased 20%. The update uses the same drilling database, with changes reflecting revised estimation methods, classification, prices, costs and reporting cut-offs. Barite and zinc are excluded, and gold is reported separately.
Apollo’s next work includes metallurgical and geotechnical drilling, water and power arrangements and environmental studies ahead of a prefeasibility study. The company expects to file the supporting technical report for the assessment by Dec. 13.

1969 Ford Cobra Barn Find Has a Rare Performance Option We All Love
18 photos
Photo: eBay/gregwill16
The Cobra name first appeared on a car when Carroll Shelby debuted his Ford-powered roadster in 1962 . Six years later, Ford debuted a high-performance engine called the Cobra Jet. The name also resurfaced on a series of limited-edition Mustangs in the 1990s. But did you know that Ford also used it on a short-lived muscle car?
In 1968, Ford launched the Torino. It was a premium sub-series of the Fairlane. The following year, Ford expanded the lineup with two models, a two-door Sportsroof (fastback) and a two-door hardtop. These cars are known as Torino Cobras or even Fairlane Cobras. Ford, however, sold them as Cobras, without Torino or Fairlane badges.
But the Cobra was more than just a Torino with a sleeker roofline. It was actually a stripped-down muscle developed to compete with the Plymouth Road Runner. The latter debuted in 1968, selling over 44,000 units. And while the regular Torino came standard with an inline-six, the Cobra rolled off the assembly line with the 428-cubic-inch (7.0-liter) Cobra Jet.
A carryover engine from 1968, when it debuted mid-model-year, the Cobra Jet came with 335 horsepower and 440 pound-feet (597 Nm) of torque. It was Ford's most potent mill except for the 429-cubic-inch Boss V8 (375 horsepower), which was only available in the Mustang for NASCAR homologation purposes.
Much like the Mustang, the Cobra also got the Super Cobra Jet option. Included in the Drag Pak bundle, the Super Cobra Jet added cast pistons, special connecting rods, an oil cooler, and the option to select a 4.30:1-ratio rear end. These features made the Cobra more suitable for drag racing.
But the Ford Cobra was never as popular as the Road Runner. While the Mopar moved over 80,000 units in 1969, Cobra sales barely exceeded 11,000 examples. And most of them are still sitting in junkyards and barns, waiting for a second chance. The Gulfstream Aqua example you see here is one of those cars.
The fastback emerged in Winchester, Kentucky, and it looks like it hasn't been touched in decades . It's dusty, the front clip is weathered, while the interior is a bit messy. It's also been partially dismantled, with the drivetrain removed. However, it appears to be a solid project car over all. And the good news is that the owner still has the numbers-matching drivetrain.
He's looking to get rid of the car, and he's also offering a donor body that will supply "some of the necessary sheetmetal." The seller also compiled a long list of the "mostly original" parts. The engine has been checked to be original, but it's not 100% complete.
The seller says he's willing to sell just the body or only certain components (hence the list in the ad), but I'd sure like to see this 1969 Cobra purchased as is and restored. And I'll give you a good reason for that too: the Ford is much rarer than the overall production number suggests.
The four-speed gearbox makes it one of only 3,910 units built, while the Gulfstream Aqua color narrows it down to just 230 examples. If we also factor in the 3.91 Traction-Lok rear axle and the front bench seat, we're probably looking at one of fewer than 100 units built like this. The seller wants $27,500 for the whole car, but he's accepting offers. What's your take on this sticker?

BYD’s upcoming multi-purpose vehicle (MPV) was spotted on a car carrier and at one of its Flash Charging stations ahead of its expected debut later this year.
BYD prepares to launch the Ocean MPV
Spy images of BYD’s new Ocean MPV testing in China have begun flooding the internet over the past few days.
BYD first unveiled the Ocean-V concept at the 2026 Beijing Auto Show in April, a futuristic preview of its first MPV under the Ocean series.
The concept featured a sliding center display screen and two unique modes: Camping and Movie. In camping mode, the seats either fold flat to create a bed or swivel to face each other.

Movie mode, on the other hand, transforms the vehicle into a private mobile theater with a large display screen that flips out of the dashboard.
With exciting features and a futuristic design, many couldn’t wait to see what the production version would look like.
The prototype spotted in testing is a bit disappointing. Although it’s still disguised, the image from Autohome shows a vehicle that looks very different from the Ocean-V concept earlier this year.
BYD Ocean MPV test car (Source: Autohome)
The image shows a boxy design with a wide grille and traditional pull-style door handles, which looks drastically different from BYD’s latest vehicles.
Spotted at a BYD Flash Charger in China, the vehicle was equipped with a massive roof-mounted LiDAR. A video (shown below) of the new model on a car carrier from ThinkerCar offers a closer look.
Local reports suggest the Ocean MPV will be 5,145 mm long, 1,970 mm wide, and 1,805 mm tall, with a 3,045 mm wheelbase. It’s also expected to feature a 2+2+3 seating layout with room for seven passengers.
A video has just surfaced of a BYD Ocean MPV test mule. It’s still heavily camouflaged, with the exterior looking largely identical to conventional MPVs. The real question is whether the interior brings something novel. https://t.co/WydRv1jiGf pic.twitter.com/aKzOtHMJKa — ThinkerCar (@thinkercar) October 28, 2026
BYD has yet to confirm any powertrain or battery specs, but given the massive grille up front, the Ocean minivan is expected to use BYD’s DM-i plug-in hybrid system and its Blade Batteries.
BYD’s current MPV lineup includes the Denza D9, a flagship model that starts above 300,000 yuan ($45,000), and the Xia, priced in the 200,000 to 300,000 yuan ($30,000 to $45,000) range. The Ocean MPV is expected to fill the gap.
Zhang Zhou, general manager of BYD’s Ocean series, said the company expects to launch its first MPV by the end of 2026.

Rivian (RIVN) just released its Q3 2026 earnings, with revenue up 38% year-over-year to $2.155 billion. The R2, in its first full quarter of deliveries, is already the company’s best-selling vehicle, ahead of both the R1 and the Amazon van.
The results beat Wall Street’s expectations, and Rivian is raising its 2026 guidance on every metric. But the car business is still losing money, and the R2 ramp made the automotive margin worse this quarter.
Rivian Q3 2026 by the numbers
We already had the volume side. Rivian reported earlier this month that it built 19,751 vehicles and delivered 19,248 in the quarter, both records. Deliveries were up 46% from a year ago and 58% from Q2.
Here’s the rest of the quarter:
Advertisement - scroll for more content
Revenue: $2.155 billion (+38% YoY)
Automotive revenue: $1.550 billion (+36%)
Software and services revenue: $605 million (+45%)
Gross profit: $176 million (8% margin)
Adjusted EBITDA: -$435 million (vs. -$602 million a year ago)
Net loss: -$913 million
Adjusted EPS: -$0.48
Free cash flow: -$1.124 billion
Cash and short-term investments: $5.502 billion
Analysts were looking for about $2.02 billion in revenue, an adjusted loss of $0.61 per share, and an adjusted EBITDA loss of roughly $576 million, according to Bloomberg consensus. Rivian beat all three.
The R2 is selling, but the cars still lose money
The demand signals for the R2 are good. Rivian says reservation conversion for the launch edition trim stayed above its expectations, it added a second R2 production shift in Normal, Illinois, and demo drives jumped to over 103,000 in the quarter, up from 57,000 in Q2.
The problem is the automotive gross margin. Rivian’s automotive segment posted an $80 million gross loss in Q3, a -5% margin. That’s better than the $130 million loss a year ago, but worse than the $36 million loss (-3%) we saw in Q2 .
Rivian blames about $120 million of extra cost of revenue on the R2 ramp, compared to production at “more normalized levels.” And the quarter got help that won’t repeat on demand: $81 million in regulatory credit revenue and an IEEPA tariff refund receivable.
Strip out the credits and the automotive segment lost about $161 million at the gross level, or roughly $8,400 per vehicle delivered. Not great.
But there’s real progress under that. Rivian says automotive cost of goods sold per unit fell by more than $12,000 quarter-over-quarter thanks to the higher R2 mix and better fixed-cost leverage. Our own math from the filing puts it at about $84,700 per vehicle in Q3, down from $96,700 in Q2. Revenue per vehicle is coming down too, which is the point of a cheaper car: about $76,300 excluding credits, versus $85,000 in Q2.
Volkswagen is carrying the gross profit
The only reason Rivian posted a consolidated gross profit is its software and services segment, which brought in $605 million in revenue and $256 million in gross profit, a 42% margin.
Of that segment revenue, $354 million (59%) came from the joint venture with Volkswagen Group, which pays Rivian for electrical architecture and software development work. Rivian says it expects to recognize that revenue through about mid-2028. Autonomy+, the paid driver-assist package launched in April, is also in there, and Rivian says take rates are “trending ahead of our expectations.”
Guidance goes up, capex comes down
Rivian updated its 2026 outlook:
Deliveries: 67,000 to 70,000 (from 65,000 to 70,000)
Adjusted EBITDA: -$1.85 billion to -$1.75 billion (improved by $100 million at the midpoint)
Capital expenditures: $1.40 billion to $1.50 billion (down $300 million at the midpoint)
With 41,807 deliveries through September, Rivian needs between 25,193 and 28,193 in Q4 to land in the new range. That would be another record by a wide margin. Rivian is providing this guidance a month into the quarter, which gives strong confidence it will hit at leat the lower end of that target.
The capex cut is about “timing of spend,” not savings. Phase 1 of the Georgia plant, which is supposed to add 300,000 units of annual capacity for R2 and R3, is still under construction.
On cash, Rivian ended the quarter with $5.502 billion, or $7.095 billion in total liquidity once you add its credit facility and the $1 billion term loan Volkswagen funded in October. That’s after the $1.5 billion share sale in July . Free cash flow was -$1.124 billion in Q3 alone.
On autonomy, Rivian still plans a limited rollout of “Point to Point” driving through an invitation-only early access program later this year, with a general release to Autonomy+ subscribers in 2027. It also says an Uber milestone expected by year-end would unlock another $250 million equity investment. More details are promised at its Autonomy and AI Day on December 9.
Electrek’s Take
This is a good quarter for Rivian, and the R2 is clearly working. Becoming the best-selling Rivian within one full quarter, while the ramp is still early, is about as good a start as you could ask for. We saw the R2 roll off the line in April , and the demand side has held up since.
But be careful with the headline beat. A lot of it came from outside the car business: Volkswagen’s checks, regulatory credits, and a one-time tariff refund. The thing Rivian actually builds and sells lost more money at the gross level than it did last quarter.
The number we care about most is the $12,000 drop in cost per vehicle. If that keeps going as the second shift fills and the $120 million in ramp costs fade, the automotive segment can get to breakeven on its own. If it stalls, Rivian is a software contractor for VW with a money-losing car company attached.
I am betting on the former. With a shift added right before the quarter started, production will likely increase significantly in Q4, and Rivian already has strong visibility into demand a month into the quarter.
If anything, I’m impressed by the demand Rivian is seeing for the more expensive launch edition of the R2. It bodes well for the cheaper version, as long as it manages to get its cost down over the coming months.

DZR Is Back As Drift: The Minna Reminds Us Who Carries the Torch of Stylish SPD-Compatible Sneakers
24 photos
Photo: Drift Sports
If you ride a bike regularly, the chances that you encounter tarmac, gravel, trails, mud, and dust, are very high, sometimes, even in the same day. But you probably want to look decent enough to still grab a coffee with the crew before or after the ride, not to mention avoiding sounding like you’re walking around on horseshoes.
That leaves most all-round riders choosing the commonly encountered two-bolt SPD-compatible sneaker, offered by numerous brands these days. But it wasn’t always like this. Back in the day, I can remember going out for a ride in the middle of the Arizona desert and having to stay in my damn boots all day. The first thing I wanted to do was take them off at the first chance I got, and often did.
Photo: Drift Sports So, back in 2010, DZR (Drift Zone Racing) arrived on the scene , and sought to change all, and if I may, by God, they succeeded; DZR had entered the market by offering the first SPD-compatible sneaker and ones that looked hella good too, even setting a trend. Modern times list countless brands that provide what they feel is the true all-rounder shoe for cyclists.
The goal was to create a shoe that could handle being taken on trails just as much as it could be seen cranking it out on asphalt, and once they managed to show the world the ‘middle ground’ well, the rest is history.
But, after 14 years of providing “stylish” all-round footwear for cyclists, DZR decided to take a bit of a break, a break where they went back to the drawing board to reimagine the next generation of SPD kicks.
Well, they came back and not just with a redesigned lineup of pumps, but also, under a new name: Drift. The reemergence happened in April 2026, and since then, two pairs of kicks have been made available under the Drift name: the Arc, the one that brought them back on the market, and the Minna. The latter is the more affordable of the bunch and the ones that remind us of most of the former DZR shoes.
Photo: Drift Sports The Minna is a model that DZR ran with for several years, and I've added a few images to the gallery so that you can compare and contrast the generations.
Now, Drift continues the tradition that put them on the map in the first place, building shoes from the ground up by hand and doing so in limited numbers or “ small batches .”
The upper to the Minna is made with textile and suede upper while the outsole is good old rubber, with the two materials holding a reinforced toe cap in place. The shank is a stiff, composite one, helping you drive all your power into your pedals and supporting the cleat.
Yet one of the most important traits of the fresh Minna is the waterproof lining integrated into the shoe. This is an essential feature if you’re looking to ride on without worrying about the terrain you’re riding through or, if you’re walking your steed, where you step. Did I mention no longer needing to bring extra pairs of socks along on the rides or trudging it out with pruned toes that eventually turn into blisters?
Photo: Drift Sports Clearly, there are some limits to how waterproof a shoe can be, and stepping into a puddle up to your ankle is bound to push those limits, but Drift does mention that their shoes have been tested in wet trail conditions and even “ steady rain ” to ensure you’re not playing around on a mini slip-and-slide in your shoes.
Ventilation is also part of the story here and holes are visible over the toes and along the sides. I’m so curious to see how these babies perform because Drift recently approached us and asked if we’d like to give them a run; my answer was a clear “Yes!” This means we will be reviewing these kicks soon, and hopefully, while riding a very exciting new beast from a brand that I can’t mention just yet; I signed an NDA.
On the underside of the Minna we can also spot a change in comparison to previous generations. The older models had a continuous tread design from toe to heel, but for the new Minna, I noticed the tip of the soles have an angled surface, helping provide crucial grip when stepping on anything with limited and minimal space; they’re “ optimized for high traction on slick trails, pump tracks, and city streets .”
Photo: Drift Sports The recessed cleat continues to provide the same all-round use, suitable for clipping in but also stepping onto a classic pedal if you bought the shoes first and will have to wait till next month to buy the pedals.
Tracks to adjust your cleat are there, and covers are sure to also be on the menu (the Arc has them), even though Drift’s website doesn’t make a mention of the latter; I’ll check in with them and update the article once we have an answer.
Oh, and if you are looking for a starting point on the whole pedal journey, Drift has a little text on their website that compares three pedal pairs on the market and scores them. Have a look.
That’s for some of the technical side of the story, but one trait that borders on technical and aesthetics is the lace cover that the new Minna has in store; I don’t see it on the older models, and since I've never tested them, I don’t know how previous generations felt with loose laces or the Velcro straps.
Photo: Drift Sports But, the latest Minna has that integrated cover that neatly clicks into the tongue, and from what I can see, keeping your laces tucked in and free from your drivetrain. They also give the shoe a slightly skate-shoe-like look. Clean.
Speaking of looks, Shane Rattazzi, Drift Co-Founder and CEO, states that, “ The Minna respects our heritage in the SPD-compatible sneaker category with modern textile and suede blends to offer a more relaxed, versatile fit for everyday progression on and off the mountain ,” and the low-top look clearly contributes to even being able to wear these babies to a job interview, as long as they’re not filthy with mud.
As for the price for a pair of these babies, Drift mentions a rate of $190 (€170) for a pair of Minnas in any of the four colors.
Is the new Minna the perfect all-round SPD shoe? I’d say it depends on the wearer, but if we consider that this crew is THE godfather of this style of kicks, there should be no doubt that there’s something special going on here. We’re about to find out.

Posted By: Cecilia Jamasmie October 29, 2026
Rio Tinto (NYSE, LSE, ASX: RIO) has marked the opening of two lithium projects in Argentina backed by about $1.4 billion (C$2 billion) in combined investment, adding capacity as it expands its battery metals business.
The Fénix 1B expansion and Sal de Vida operation in Catamarca province achieved first production in the second quarter ahead of schedule and are ramping up output, the company disclosed Thursday . Together, they will add 25,000 tonnes of annual lithium carbonate equivalent (LCE) capacity once fully operational.
“These two projects build on nearly three decades of lithium production in Catamarca and the expertise of our Argentine workforce,” CEO Simon Trott said in a release. President Javier Milei and Catamarca Governor Raúl Jalil attended the inauguration.
The early production starts haven’t ensured a smooth ramp-up. In its Oct. 14 operating review, Rio reported slower-than-expected progress at Sal de Vida because of equipment availability. The company expected annual lithium output at the low end of its 61,000-to-64,000-tonne LCE guidance range, mainly because of that delay.
Rio is targeting global annual capacity of 200,000 tonnes LCE by 2028.
Expanding production
Fénix 1B adds 10,000 tonnes of annual LCE capacity, increasing the operation’s total target to about 40,000 tonnes.
Rio is evaluating a further expansion at Fénix that would require about $1 billion in additional investment. A final investment decision on the proposed Fénix II plant at the Hombre Muerto salt flat could come towards the end of the decade, Trott told Reuters .
The company plans to submit Fénix II next year to Argentina’s Large Investment Incentive Regime (RIGI), which offers long-term tax and regulatory benefits, according to the news agency.
Fénix began production in 1997 as Argentina’s first commercial lithium operation.
Sal de Vida, a new lithium carbonate operation about 20 km northeast of Fénix, has a target annual capacity of 15,000 tonnes LCE.
Rio inherited both operations through its March 2025 acquisition of Arcadium Lithium .
Fénix uses direct lithium extraction (DLE), while Sal de Vida relies on conventional evaporation ponds. DLE separates lithium from brine without prolonged solar concentration.
France’s Eramet (ENX: ERA) also deployed DLE at its Centenario-Ratones operation in Salta province, where first lithium carbonate production was achieved in December 2024 .
Fénix, Sal de Vida and Olaroz have combined target capacity of 97,500 tonnes LCE annually on a whole-operation basis, before adjusting for Rio’s ownership interests.
Rio’s Argentine portfolio includes a 66.5% stake in Olaroz in Jujuy and full ownership of Rincón in Salta, alongside its Catamarca operations.
The company is also exploring opportunities to advance copper projects in Argentina, Trott told Reuters .
Investment incentives
“The expansion of the Fénix project is a historic milestone that demonstrates the potential of Argentina’s mining sector,” Milei said in Rio’s release. “This was made possible by the country once again creating incentives for the production of resources that are essential to the modern world.”
Rio expects to spend about 70% of its planned $4 billion in Argentine lithium growth capital with local suppliers.
RIGI provides 30-year fiscal and regulatory stability for qualifying projects, with a general minimum investment of $200 million.
Argentina’s lithium exports generated $1.62 billion in the first nine months of this year, up 173% from a year earlier, according to the Mining Secretariat’s October export report . Export volumes increased 45% over the same period.
Argentina, Bolivia and Chile form South America’s Lithium Triangle, a region with large lithium-bearing brine deposits.
Benchmark Mineral Intelligence is forecasting that global lithium demand will rise from 2.11 million tonnes LCE this year to about 7 million tonnes by 2050, led by electric vehicles and energy storage.
Argentina’s Mining Secretariat projects the country could overtake Chile in lithium production around 2029 and reach about 573,000 tonnes LCE annually by 2035.
Rio’s Rincón expansion is targeting first production in 2028, followed by a three-year ramp-up towards 60,000 tonnes of annual capacity. Print

Okay, Which One of You Ordered This Cool Lamborghini Urus SE Performante With Ad Personam Touches?
8 photos
Photo: Instagram | Lamborghini
What is the latest and greatest Lamborghini in your vision? Could it be the Temerario “baby” supercar? The Revuelto flagship? The Fenomeno that’s part of the company’s “few-off” series? Or the Urus?
Well, it all depends on what you like, to be honest, but from a financial perspective, it is none other than the latter. After all, this model, which is the brand’s second high-rider after the iconic LM002 manufactured between 1986 and 1993, has helped the Raging Bull more than double its sales, proving that exotic crossovers can be extremely successful if they are marketed correctly.
Overall, the Lamborghini Urus is an aging product. That’s because it will turn ten in 2017. It hit the assembly line back in 2017, and when the facelifted iteration came out five years later, the lineup was expanded with the Urus S and Urus Performante. Then the Urus SE came out with its plug-in hybrid powertrain, boasting plenty of oomph.
It had 789 hp (800 ps/589 kW) in total and 701 lb-ft (950 Nm) of torque, taking 3.4 seconds from 0-62 mph (0-100 kph), and maxing out at 194 mph (312 kph). But why are we talking about it in past tense? For a very simple reason: the Urus SE is dead. And it’s also buried. And it will remain that way for eternity, because Lamborghini has a new member in the Urus family.
It is called the Lamborghini Urus SE Performante , and it is the automaker’s most powerful crossover ever made. The model debuted back when it was still summer in the northern hemisphere, retiring its predecessor, and remaining the only Urus currently in production.
Photo: Instagram | Lamborghini As you likely recall, it has 801 horsepower available via the right pedal in total, which equals 812 metric horsepower and 597 kilowatts. The peak torque is officially rated at 738 pound-feet (1,000 Nm). That’s a 12 hp (12 ps/9 kW) boost over the Urus SE, and 144 hp (146 ps/107 kW) more than the Urus S and Urus Performante. Compared to the original iteration, the new PHEV model is 160 hp (162 ps/119 kW) more powerful.
It features a twin-turbocharged 4.0-liter V8 engine with plug-in hybrid capabilities. The electric motor is housed inside the ZF eight-speed automatic transmission. Lamborghini’s Urus SE Performante takes 3.3 seconds from 0 to 62 mph. Thus, it is just as fast as the old Urus Performante, and 0.1 seconds quicker than the Urus SE. It has a 194 mph ()312 kph) top speed, and can travel 37 miles (60 km) on electric power alone.
Now, despite being a few months old, the Lamborghini Urus SE Performante does not get much attention from the internet. But the Raging Bull knows that it is a moneymaker, and plans to make it more visible in the online kingdom. And in this case, it used its personalization division, Ad Personam, in order to put the spotlight on the example pictured in the gallery.
The vehicle in question definitely looks the part with its light blue paint finish. The color is called the Celeste Phoebe, and it is contrasted by some exposed carbon fiber elements, as well as some black touches here and there, the rear privacy windows, and the OEM wheels that are presented in Aether Shiny White, according to the automaker itself.
Photo: Instagram | Lamborghini One might expect to find an equally-colorful cockpit, right? Well, maybe if this Lamborghini Urus SE Performante came from a tuner. But it was signed by Ad Personam, as mentioned above, and in this case, it features a black cabin with some white accents for contrast, including the stitching, the special touches on the seats, and the Performante embroidery on the seatbacks.
Overall, this is a very eye-catching product, this writer believes, albeit one that deserves to celebrate its fifteen minutes of online fame sitting under more natural light. What I am trying to say is that the clouds should take some time off in order to let the sun bathe it as it should.
Moreover, Ad Personam proves yet again that those who want to make their Lamborghini vehicles stand out more do not need to turn to the tuning world, because the Raging Bull’s personalization division has plenty of aces up its sleeve, and in the right combination, you won’t encounter an identical ride.
Sure, interested parties will have to reach out to tuners if more power is what they want, because Ad Personam only takes care of the visuals both inside and out. But realistically speaking, does any modern-day Lambo require more oomph? That would obviously be a no, as the supercars and the latest version of the Urus pack more than enough punch for daily drives, sprinkled with the occasional run at the local racetrack.
Now, do you dig the spec of this Lamborghini Urus SE Performante ? I do, and this comes from someone who is not a fan of the model that shares its underpinnings with the demised Volkswagen Touareg, among others. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Lamborghini (@lamborghini)

source_document.body:
Artificial intelligence (AI), data centers, and electrification are increasing U.S. electricity demand. Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory estimates data centers could account for 11.8% of electricity consumption by 2030 , within a projected range of 9.5%–15.3%. The U.S. Energy Information Administration (EIA) forecasts electricity consumption to increase by approximately 2.2% in 2026 and a further 1.6% in 2027. While new generation and transmission infrastructure will help meet demand, existing plants must continue delivering a reliable base load.
Nuclear energy supplied approximately 18% of U.S. utility-scale electricity in 2025, with an average fleet capacity factor of 91%. Maintaining that contribution depends not only on reactor systems but also on steam generators, feedwater piping, turbines, and other balance-of-plant equipment. Inspection-led maintenance, along with appropriately qualified repairs and protection, can help preserve reliability.
The Reliability Value of the Existing Nuclear Fleet
As of March 2026, the U.S. had 94 operating commercial reactors at 54 sites, averaging approximately 44 years of age. Many have already received license extensions beyond their original 40-year terms, and subsequent renewals may permit operation for up to 80 years , subject to Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) review and aging-management requirements. These longer operating lives increase the importance of monitoring equipment degradation and intervening before defects require extensive corrective work. Life extension does not mean retaining every component indefinitely. Operators must distinguish between equipment suitable for continued monitoring, systems requiring structural repair or replacement, and sound surfaces where added protection could control a documented damage mechanism.
Nuclear plants supply large, baseload sources of electricity. A forced outage requires grid operators to secure replacement generation, potentially tightening regional supply margins and increasing costs. The consequences depend on the outage duration, regional demand, and available replacement capacity. A single reactor trip does not necessarily interrupt customer supply, but a prolonged loss can increase demand on other generating assets. For plants operating at high capacity factors, lost output is also difficult to recover later. Unexpected equipment maintenance can disrupt refueling schedules, increase specialist labor requirements, and expand future outage scopes. Predictable component condition is therefore valuable to both plant operations and grid reliability.
Managing Degradation in Steam and Feedwater Systems
In pressurized water reactors (PWRs), steam-generator tubes separate the radioactive primary system from the secondary system that produces steam for electricity generation. Corrosion, cracking, vibration and deposit buildup can damage these tubes, potentially affecting their integrity. Operators manage these risks through water chemistry control, regular inspections, and established repair procedures. Any signs of damage must be assessed against strict safety requirements.
Other components, including feedwater piping, cross-under piping, and turbine steam systems, also face deterioration. One common issue is flow-accelerated corrosion (FAC) , where flowing water or wet steam gradually wears away the protective oxide layer inside carbon-steel pipes, leading to wall thinning (Figure 1). Damage can be particularly severe around bends, joints, and areas where flow changes direction or speed. Vibration, water droplets, and temperature changes can cause further wear. Because deterioration often occurs internally, it may not be visible during routine external inspections.
1. Flow-accelerated corrosion diagram. Courtesy: IGS
The risks became clear in December 1986, when a major feedwater pipe rupture at a U.S. PWR prompted greater regulatory attention to pipe-wall thinning. Today, operators use ultrasonic inspections, monitoring, and predictive assessments to identify vulnerable areas and track deterioration. These measures help detect wall loss early, allowing repairs to be planned before equipment integrity or plant availability is affected.
Selecting Repairs and Protection According to Condition
The appropriate intervention depends on component condition, degradation mechanism, and applicable engineering requirements. Where wall thickness has fallen below acceptable limits, qualified weld build-up or component replacement may be required to restore structural integrity. Where the substrate remains fit for service, High Velocity Thermal Spray (HVTS) alloy cladding can provide long-term protection against further corrosion and erosion.
The two approaches can also be combined. Qualified welding restores lost wall thickness, while HVTS cladding can subsequently be applied over suitably prepared and inspected surfaces to provide a metallurgical upgrade and mitigate recurring degradation. This allows operators to coordinate structural restoration and longer-term protection within a single planned maintenance scope.
Unlike weld overlay, HVTS application (Figure 2) does not create a heat-affected zone in the base metal and can be completed more rapidly by eliminating post-application heat treatment requirements. Shorter application times may help operators complete maintenance work within planned outages and, where radiological controls apply, support ALARA (as low as reasonably achievable) objectives by reducing time spent in exposed work areas. The potential exposure benefit must be assessed against the full work scope, including preparation, application, and inspection.
2. HVTS application. Courtesy: IGS
As a protective alloy layer, HVTS is intended to mitigate ongoing metal wastage and support longer component service life, potentially limiting the need for repeated interventions.
Case Study: Protecting Cross-Under Piping
An application at one nuclear plant illustrates this approach. High-velocity wet steam had caused FAC and erosion in cross-under piping, particularly near turning vanes and high-flow regions. The operator sought to limit further wall loss without the disruption associated with large-scale piping replacement.
A localized HVTS trial began in 2009. In a wider life-extension assessment initiated in 2018, the plant evaluated pipe replacement, weld overlay, and HVTS cladding. Inspections identified priority locations (Figure 3), allowing the operator to divide surface protection work into planned outage scopes. Existing protection was removed where required, and engineered HVTS alloy cladding was applied to selected surfaces where the piping was suitable for continued service. This enabled the operator to focus on vulnerable regions rather than treat all piping identically, while coordinating preparation, application, and inspection with other outage activities.
3. Application areas and phased scope. Courtesy: IGS
The project involved approximately 8,000 ft 2 (740 m 2 ) of treatment per unit across two units, delivered through a phased four-year program. Annual application areas ranged from approximately 850 ft 2 to 3,000 ft 2 (79 m 2 to 279 m 2 ), with no additional outage days required. Long-term performance has also been demonstrated, with cladding applied during an initial trial in 2009 reported to be in excellent condition after more than 15 years of service.
The case demonstrates how inspection, targeted protection, and phased execution can support longer equipment life while preserving planned outage schedules. It does not constitute a precedent for automatic approval at U.S. plants, where each application needs its own technical and quality assessment. Nor should the service record of a trial area be assumed to predict performance across every location or operating environment.
Turning Equipment Integrity into More Predictable Generation
For nuclear operators, effective asset integrity management starts with linking inspection results, operating history, and remaining-life assessments to a prioritized maintenance plan. Steam-generator tubing, FAC-prone piping, and turbine steam-system wear require distinct inspection and intervention strategies rather than a single treatment approach.
Planning ahead of outages allows time to establish repair designs, procedures, materials, quality controls, and access arrangements. Using inspection trends to define the scope early also reduces the risk of discovering extensive work only after the unit has been taken offline. It also helps differentiate components needing replacement or structural restoration from sound surfaces that may benefit from protection. Where work takes place in radiologically controlled areas, crew size, time on task, and the potential for repeat exposure should inform execution planning.
Capital allocation also benefits from this distinction. Measured degradation rates can show where a localized intervention is technically justified and where wholesale replacement is unavoidable. This helps operators prioritize expenditure according to component condition and expected operational benefit, rather than treating every susceptible circuit as requiring the same scope of work.
Operators can assess the contribution of these decisions through forced-loss rates, unit availability, outage schedule adherence, and repeat degradation findings. These measures connect component-level maintenance to the wider objective of dependable generation without displacing safety and regulatory requirements.
Maintaining a Reliable Fleet
As U.S. electricity demand rises, preserving the performance of existing nuclear assets remains essential alongside investment in new capacity. Early inspection, correctly matched repairs, and suitably qualified surface protection can limit recurring degradation and reduce avoidable outage work. Maintaining steam and feedwater system integrity therefore supports the long-term availability of America’s nuclear fleet.
—Keith Reeser is senior director with IGS, and Craig Herbster is nuclear corrosion subject matter expert with IGS.

TFI International has tried to get investors to take notice of its Truckload operations, which are substantial but smaller than its more better-known LTL segment. The third quarter results may be the catalyst that gets that recognition to occur.
Where the third quarter LTL segment at TFI (NYSE: TFII) saw its operating ratio rise compared to a year ago, the OR for Truckload strengthened. And it was the Truckload operations that led CEO Alain Bedard’s comments in the prepared statement released Thursday afternoon along with its earnings.
Bedard described Truckload as having a “remarkably strong” quarter. “Our Truckload performance is particularly gratifying, with double digit top line growth despite fewer trucks and operating income that nearly doubled,” Bedard said.
The overall impact of the higher LTL OR and the much improved truckload OR led to a company-wide OR of 89.5% compared to 91.2% from a year ago.
The Truckload segment had operating income of $100.2 million, up 13.3% from a year ago, while LTL’s operating income was $44.4 million, up 6.6%. A year ago, LTL’s operating income was $77.7 million while Truckload was $52.6 million.
TFI’s Logistics segment had operating income that surpassed LTL, coming in at $49.4 million.
Diluted EPS of $1.28, compared to $1.02 a year earlier, is expected to be surpassed in the fourth quarter, TFI said, projecting EPS for the three months to be between $1.30 to $1.40.
Several of the LTL metrics fell sharply, leading to the deterioration in adjusted OR. Revenue per hundred weight excluding fuel, the key yield figure, declined less than 1%. But revenue per shipment excluding fuel fell 22%.
The average weight per shipment was down 3.58%. TFI did see its total LTL shipments rise 4.62%.
With year-ago comparisons on revenue in Truckload impacted by the weak freight market of 2025, Truckload revenue rose 142.1%. But adjusted EBITDA in Truckload was up 24.7% and operating income rose more than 90%.
The Truckload segment was much smaller in size than a year ago, with the truck count down almost 12%. The number of owner operators also declined about 4.8%.
TFI International’s earnings call with analysts will be Friday at 9:30 am EDT.

Toyota’s EV sales have jumped 127% through September, but that isn’t telling the whole story. Slumping demand for gas and hybrid cars in China has pushed global sales lower for three months in a row.
Toyota’s EV sales rise, but China drags on global results
Including Lexus, Toyota sold 309,766 battery electric vehicles (BEVs) globally through the first nine months of 2026, up 127.4% from the same period last year.
Except for January (+87.5%), Toyota’s EV sales have more than doubled every month this year compared with 2025.
The higher demand comes after Toyota and Lexus launched updated versions of their first-gen electric SUVs, the bZ4X (now the bZ in the US) and the RZ.
Advertisement - scroll for more content
Toyota has added several new electric models, including the C-HR+ (C-HR in the US), bZ4X Touring (bZ Woodland in the US), and Urban Cruiser, while Lexus now offers the ES EV. Both brands will introduce a three-row electric SUV, which is expected to go on sale over the next few months.
According to data from Cleantechnica , the Toyota bZ4X became the 20th best-selling EV worldwide through August, with nearly 100,000 units sold.
Toyota bZ Limited (Source: Toyota Canada)
While its EVs are catching on, Toyota Motor’s global sales fell for the third straight month in September.
Toyota sold 860,107 vehicles in September, down 2.2% from the previous year. The company said that although overall demand remained steady, sales in China fell, leading to lower overall sales than last year.
From left to right: Toyota’s new C-HR+, bZ4X, and Urban Cruiser electric SUVs (Source: Toyota Europe)
Through September, Toyota sold 7.51 million vehicles globally, down 3.4%. In China, Toyota’s sales plunged nearly 20%, marking its eighth consecutive month with lower sales.
Toyota said the overall market in China “remained weak due in part to rising gasoline prices, while the market for gasoline vehicles and hybrid vehicles was particularly affected,” resulting in lower sales.
Toyota bZ7 (Source: Toyota)
In the first nine months of 2026, Toyota sold just over 1.05 million vehicles in China, 18.9% fewer than in the same period last year.
Toyota sells several electric vehicles through its two joint ventures (GAC Toyota and FAW Toyota) in China, including the bZ3, bZ3X, bZ5, and bZ7.
Electrek’s Take
After the US, China is Toyota’s second-largest market. Through September, Toyota has now sold more vehicles in its home market of Japan (1.19 million) than in China.
To turn things around and compete with companies like BYD, Toyota, like many major OEMs nowadays, is increasingly adopting more Chinese EV tech and manufacturing practices.
Nikkei reported in August that Toyota plans to build a new Lexus electric SUV in China, rather than in Japan as it has traditionally. Production is expected to begin at Lexus’ new manufacturing plant in Shanghai next fall.
The new Lexus EV will use advanced manufacturing methods, including gigacasting, to cut costs and speed up production.
Toyota isn’t the only legacy automaker struggling to keep pace in China’s fast-moving automotive market.
Volkswagen Group CFO and COO, Arno Antilitz, admitted the company “must act quickly and decisively” after reporting third-quarter sales in China dropped 38% to 405,800 units on Thursday. The company also plans to use technology developed in China for its next-gen EVs, which it will sell overseas.

76-Year-Old Lady Has Been Traveling Around in Her Tesla on FSD Only for Months
10 photos
Photo: Retired Young Now What | YouTube
A 76-year-old lady living in California feels like the queen of the road in her Tesla Model Y. She goes around running errands in her electric crossover, running exclusively on FSD after summoning it out of the garage.
This is how every drive starts, right after she unplugs the Tesla that she affectionately calls "Tessie." To bring the car out of the garage, she stands outside, taps the Tesla app on her phone, engages the Summon feature, selects "Come to Me," and the car backs out of the garage on its own. There is no way she would do this on her own. She says the space is much too tight.
She is the 76-year-old lady who proves that whoever said that senior drivers can’t adapt to new technology was terribly wrong. The driver you are looking at is impressively tech-savvy. She gets into the driver’s seat, tells Grok what she needs, taps the touchscreen, and off she goes.
Grok acts as an advanced voice-activated personal assistant inside her Tesla, allowing her to control the vehicle and manage errands entirely hands-free. At the age of 76, navigating through the menu would probably take a while. Grok is her shortcut.
Photo: Retired Young Now What | YouTube She wasn’t this chill right from the start, she tells her son, who is filming her trip from the passenger seat. Her son, Tim, is a retired law enforcement officer, proud to have a mom this tech whiz. She tells him how she took a 250-mile trip to Fortuna, California, going through mountain passes and upgrading to Standard Mode.
She usually travels in Chill mode, which means the car specifically selects the slowest lanes, avoids overtaking, and generally provides a relaxed, cautious, and ultra-smooth ride. Standard, however, looks like the driving style of a confident person, maintaining a safe distance from vehicles in front but passing those who drive exceptionally slowly in front of it.
It may not sound like much, but for her, it is a big deal. She is just learning to yield control and feel comfortable enough to go to the next level. Once the car reaches its destination, it parks automatically, as Tim and his mom remember how it parked in the spot reserved for people with disabilities. " She only did that once, " his mother defends Tessie. That one time, she had to take over and park the car herself. She still got it!
In the meantime, the system has been learning. The 76-year-old owner has had it since July, when she traded in her 2018 Cadillac CTS. She went for the Long Range AWD Premium . Quite a technology and performance gap there!
Photo: Retired Young Now What | YouTube Her Tesla is set in motion by a dual-motor powertrain, pushing out 397 horsepower (402 metric horsepower) and 389 pound-feet (527 Newton meters) of torque for a run from 0 to 60 mph (0 to 97 kph) in 4.6 seconds and a top speed of 125 mph (201 kph).
She obviously hasn't tested the performance of her EV. It will take a while before she goes all Mad Max with her FSD. It's been three months since she has been traveling around, hardly ever touching the steering wheel. She believes Tessie is far better at driving than she is right now.
Besides, she hates driving at night because her eyesight is playing tricks on her. Having the Tesla Model Y allows her to stay out for longer in the evenings. She no longer needs to worry about driving in the dark.
She does keep her eyes on the road at all times. A camera monitors her attention every time FSD is on. However, it once insisted that she did that even though she was. The camera can easily see through prescription glasses, but dark lenses confuse it most of the time.
Photo: Retired Young Now What | YouTube But she has different standards when it comes to fun driving. " This is fun ," she says as she glances at her son and keeps her hands in her lap. She likes to be spoiled by the car. She feels chauffeured. While her former car, the Caddy, was very comfortable, it could by no means do everything her Tesla is doing for her.
Now, she is always entertained, as Tesla released the Halloween mode, the latest 2026.38 software update rolling out right now. The new mode turns pedestrians into walking skeletons or zombies, cars into ghosts, and traffic lights into glowing pumpkins. Furthermore, the blinker sounds switch from the usual click to an owl hooting.
If you would expect the viewers to criticize her, pointing out that her driving skills and reflexes aren’t quite as sharp as they used to be, many jumped into the comments section to praise her for not being stuck at home, dreaming of wandering around.

Less-than-truckload carrier Saia continued to see outsized volume growth in the third quarter as it leveraged an expanded terminal network. The period delivered record revenue and tonnage for the company, with its focus now centered on improving operating results at the new locations.
Saia’s ( NASDAQ: SAIA ) reported third-quarter earnings per share of $3.41 on Thursday before the market opened. The result was 60 cents higher y/y and 11 cents better than the consensus estimate. A $3.6-million decline in net interest expense was a 10-cent y/y tailwind.
(The comparison to the 2025 third quarter excludes a $14.5-million net impact from real estate gains and impairments, resulting in adjusted EPS of $2.81.)
Revenue of $983 million was 17% higher y/y and $15 million better than analysts’ expectations. (Diesel prices were 48% higher y/y in the quarter.)
Tonnage was up 9% y/y as shipments increased 1% and weight per shipment grew 8%. On a y/y comparison, tonnage increased 7.8% in July, 8.7% in August and 10.3% in September. Tonnage is up 10% y/y so far in October.
Since 2022, the company has opened 45 new terminals and relocated or expanded another 25. While its 219-terminal network is still smaller than other national carriers, management said the company is finally “on equal footing.”
September marked the ninth straight month of expansion for the U.S. manufacturing complex, which is a significant source of LTL freight. Also, Saia REV has reduced transit times in over 2,000 lanes, providing an additional source for “outsized volume growth.”
Table: Saia’s key performance indicators
Revenue per hundredweight (yield) was 2% lower y/y, excluding fuel surcharges. However, higher shipment weights and a 1% decline in length of haul were headwinds for the metric.
Revenue per shipment (ex-fuel) was up 6% y/y even with continued weakness in the Los Angeles market, which carries higher freight bills. The company’s national expansion and improved service give it confidence that it can push pricing and close the gap to peers.
“Frankly, the service levels that we’ve been providing … support that,” said President and CEO Fritz Holzgrefe on a Thursday call with analysts.
Saia implemented a 7.1% general rate increase on July 6, which was 120 bps higher and three months earlier than last year’s rate hike. It said the GRI is performing well and that it continues to “see great results from that.”
Contractual rate renewals averaged 10.8% in the quarter, up 15.9% on a two-year-stacked comp.
The company logged an 87.6% operating ratio (inverse of operating margin ), which was flat y/y and just 70 bps worse than the second quarter . It normally sees 150 to 200 bps of margin degradation from the second to third quarter.
The y/y comparison had the added headwind of two wage increases in the quarter. There was no pay bump in the 2025 third quarter as the increase wasn’t installed until October, while this year’s increase occurred as normal in July. Also, the new terminals are operating at a low-90% OR, but 40 bps better y/y.
It normally sees 250 to 300 bps of margin deterioration from the third to the fourth quarter, but is calling for just 200 bps of degradation this year, implying an 89.6% OR (230 bps better than the 2025 fourth-quarter unadjusted OR).
It said it will continue to lean on the cost advantage that the railroads provide.
Purchased transportation expense (as a percentage of revenue) increased 220 bps y/y. Saia’s rail and truck partners accounted for 15.7% of total linehaul miles during the quarter, but the company was able to manage outside rate-per-mile inflation to just 4%. It expects further cost inflation on purchased transportation, but noted that contracts with providers are staggered.
Saia announced a $250-million share repurchase program on Thursday. It has done most of the heavy lifting on the growth capex front. It expects capex to total 13% to 14.5% of revenue next year, with 12% to 15% the longer-term target.
Full-year net capex is now expected to total $350 million this year, down from the prior guidance range of $350 million to $400 million. Net capex was $544 million in 2025 and $1.05 billion in 2024.
It generated over $240 million in free cash flow through the third quarter and ended the period with over $100 million in net cash.
Shares of SAIA were up 3% at 2:51 p.m. EDT on Thursday compared to the S&P 500, which was down 0.6%.
Why it matters? Saia is one of a few publicly traded LTL carriers. Its quarterly results provide insight into a subsegment of trucking where few public datasets exist.

FedEx Corp. delivered strong third quarter results driven by higher volumes and pricing for premium B2B and B2C shipping services, but bullishness for peak holiday season demand was tempered by expectations for lower domestic margins amid a rise in transitory labor and outsourced trucking costs that likely will spill into next year.
Consolidated revenue grew 12% to $22.9 billion, with adjusted operating income of $1.2 billion, up 16% year over year, the freight transportation giant reported after the market closed on Wednesday, beating Wall Street expectations. Adjusted earnings per share was $3.74, up 28% from the prior year.
A quarter of FedEx’s ( NYSE: FDX ) revenue growth is attributable to higher fuel surcharges. Results also benefitted from continued structural cost reductions from network optimization initiatives. FedEx so far has closed 260 delivery stations and expects to realize $1 billion in recurring savings because of network and corporate restructuring by the end of the year, and $2 billion in savings by the end of 2027.
Network integration has been completed in large metropolitan areas like Dallas, San Francisco, Phoenix and Washington, D.C., along with Canada last year. Early next year, FedEx will tackle Los Angeles; Charlotte, North Carolina; and Oklahoma City, CEO Raj Subramaniam told analysts during a conference call about the financial results.
This is the first peak season for FedEx operating at scale under its Network 2.0 initiative to consolidate ground and express networks, with about 65% of eligible volume expected to flow through dual-purpose facilities.
FedEx revised upward its full-year outlook. Revenue is now estimated to grow 12% year over year vs the prior estimate of 11% growth and adjusted diluted earnings per share are projected at $18.30 at the midpoint range, up from $17.50.
It was FedEx’s first quarterly earnings report aligned with its new calendar-year reporting framework, following the company’s transition from a May 31 fiscal year-end to a December 31 year-end. As such, FedEx also reported four-month results to cover June, alongside normal quarterly results.
FedEx, much like UPS, has pivoted since 2024 toward high- margin sectors that require end-to-end-logistics services, such as aerospace, automotive, healthcare, and high-tech, and foregoing no-frills, local and regional last-mile delivery for cost-conscious e-commerce retailers. The AI and data center industry was the fastest growing vertical at FedEx during the quarter. A recent Frost & Sullivan report , sponsored by FedEx, discussed how AI is influencing trade patterns in the Asia-Pacific region and trans-Pacific freight movements, which FedEx is capitalizing on.
One year ago, as part of the focus on revenue quality, the company began offering more tailored services for the automotive production market, with a dedicated team, 24/7 support, flexible global pickup capabilities, and enhanced visibility. The effort paid off in the third quarter when it began serving 13 major automotive customers, Chief Commercial Officer Brie Carere said.
FedEx’s realignment of airline operations is also playing a key role in creating a better value proposition for customers, according to management. Under the Tricolor initiative, running parallel to optimization of the North American surface transportation network, the integrated logistics company essentially segregates overnight express parcels from deferred pallet shipments to better utilize aircraft and workforces, with the goal of creating better density, reducing cost and attracting high-value heavyweight cargo from logistics service providers.
Average daily freight pounds grew 15% year-over-year and FedEx is winning share in the air freight market, indicating that the approach towards heavyweight, premium service is paying off, management said. Rival DHL Express is similarly pursuing a strategy of pursuing more heavy freight to fill out available space on package aircraft.
“Our expanding capabilities across key verticals are enabling us to address more of our customers’ logistic needs, unlocking air freight demand from traditionally parcel-centric customers. For example, we drove a 15-fold increase in aircraft engine moves and won new air freight business with an AI data center customer after more than a 40-year largely parcel-centric relationship,” Subramaniam said during the briefing. “Differentiation is increasingly centered on deep customer relationships and tailored service experiences, positioning us to capture more freight volume as we address customers’ needs beyond parcel.”
Domestic
Revenue for the domestic business increased 10% year over year, supported by a 2% gain in average daily package volume. Adjusted operating margins ticked down 20 basis points to 6.6% due to the negative impact of higher costs for fuel and purchased transportation, offsetting savings from network restructuring.
The 4% volume decline for the home delivery Ground Economy product was intentional as FedEx price hikes discouraged budget-conscious retailers from
Management expressed confidence for a good peak season, with revenue projected to be up 10% quarter over quarter, noting that the top 30 customers are planning for about 2% growth in average daily parcel volume from Black Friday through Christmas.
Rising costs could slow profit growth in the fourth quarter. FedEx outsources about 10% of its linehaul and executives said they anticipated about $130 million in higher expenses month over month due to elevated rates in the truckload sector, where capacity is very tight. The company will incrementally insource more linehaul operations next year and take specific commercial pricing actions to address the cost challenges. TD Cowen analyst Jason Seidl suggested FedEx is also likely to shift some volume to railroads, where intermodal costs are lower than truckload.
FedEx also faces pressure from its new pilot contract, with about $100 million of above- normal wage inflation quarterly expected through 2027 and an $80 million increase in aircraft maintenance expense versus the fourth quarter of 2025 because more aircraft are due for comprehensive, heavy inspections.
Management said it expects more bottom line capture of revenue from recently announced peak season surcharges and a 5.9% general rate increase next year.
International
Express international revenue increased 17%, primarily due to higher fuel surcharges, higher pricing for packages and freight, and growth in overseas export and freight volumes. Margins were up 4% year over year.
International freight revenue grew 28%, helped by the data center vertical.
International economy and freight segments experienced strong volumes arising from recovery in the U.S.-China trade lane, which declined last because of the trade war between the countries, and demand from large-scale cloud service and technology companies. Low-yield U.S. exports were down 11% in the third quarter. FedEx next year is likely to squeeze out less desirable freight with higher pricing to improve margins, Seidl said in a client note.
FedEx is also consolidating its fragmented country operations in Europe to make it easier for customers to manage shipments across an integrated network across borders. In France, the company has closed 17 stations, modernized two hubs and 16 stations by installing advanced, automated sorting systems, and equipped 32 stations with new tracking and monitoring technology, said Subramaniam.
In Italy, FedEx is similarly simplifying operations to prioritize higher-value international B2B and export services. As part of this process, FedEx is transitioning from an eight-hub footprint to a highly streamlined three-hub footprint and actively reducing station count, the CEO said. In June, the company reached an important milestone when it consolidated two Milan area stations into a newly upgraded facility that allows more efficient pickup and delivery within one of the most densely populated areas of the country.
FedEx plans to reduce domestic capacity by 20% in Italy by 20%, 30% in the United Kingdom and 40% in France. “The second part of our strategy is to improve the mix. Given the network utilization, we are now focusing our commercial teams on driving more intercontinental and intra-European volume and reducing lower-yielding intra-country volume,” Subramaniaam said.
The integrator is on track to reach its target of $650 million in adjusted operating income in Europe by the end of 2029, he added.
FedEx said it has returned the majority of its MD-11 tri-engine freighters to service after fixing a design flaw , per Boeing instructions, that had the potential to allow fatigue cracks in the engine pylon. U.S. authorities forced operators to ground their fleets for several months following the fatal crash last November of an MD-11 operated by UPS.
Adjusted results exclude $270 million in costs related to expenses for network restructuring or the spin off of FedEx Freight last summer. FedEx rewarded investors by using some of its profits to buy back $2 billion in shares during the quarter.
FedEx earlier this month completed the sale of its contract logistics unit, FedEx Supply Chain, to France-based shipping and logistics giant CMA CGM for $1.4 billion as it focuses on its core freight transportation business.
Meanwhile, consortium of investors is nearing the completion of the $9.2 billion InPost deal, which will give FedEx a 37% share in the European express delivery company and greater opportunities in the B2C parcel sector without having to divert resources from core B2B operations.
Earlier this week, FedEx announced the appointment of AutoZone executive Jamere Jackson as its next chief financial officer.
Equity analysts continue to recommend FedEx, citing volume growth trends and higher profit margins once the U.S. ground network is fully merged next year and streamlining efforts in Europe take root. FedEx stock price was up less than a point to $307.08 a share in late day trading on Thursday.

Driver of Ram 1500 SRT TRX Says He Got People Rolling Their Eyes at Him
14 photos
Photo: ThatDudeinBlue | YouTube
The Ram 1500 SRT TRX is the world's most powerful truck with an internal combustion engine, and you’ve got the HEMI to thank for it. But how is living with such an absurdly powerful vehicle? The man who got to spend a week with it gives an honest review and tells about how he had to help his mother into the cabin and how some roll their eyes when they see him driving the TRX.
Let's do numbers first, because that is where it all begins. The Ram 1500 SRT TRX made a comeback together with the HEMI that former Stellantis CEO Carlos Tavares decided to pull the plug on back in 2023. But with Tavares out of the game and Tim Kuniskis back in , the HEMI returned more powerful than it was when it was discontinued.
So now, Ram’s almighty T-Rex truck comes with the beloved 6.2-liter HEMI V8 with supercharged firepower, now pushing out 777 horsepower (788 metric horsepower) and 680 pound-feet (922 Newton meters) of torque.
That is what makes it rocket from zero to hero (0 to 60 mph or 0 to 97 kph) in 3.5 seconds, flash down the quarter mile in 12.2 seconds with a trap speed of 177 kph, and max out at 118 mph (190 kph), an electronic limit set due to the off-road speed rating of its 35-inch tires. A TorqueFlite 8HP95 8-speed automatic transmission puts the power down through all four corners.
Photo: ThatDudeinBlue | YouTube This is what David Patterson of the ThatDudeinBlue YouTube channel is dealing with since he drove home in the brand-new Ram 1500 SRT TRX for the week of testing. Now, he breaks down the truck's performance, real-world perks and downsides, along with how he feels on board.
Obnoxious, silly, and ridiculous. This is how he describes the truck. First things first: getting into the truck can be a start on the wrong foot because the steps aren't of much help. Olympic gymnast skills would definitely help, but that’s something that David’s mother doesn’t have. So David and his father had to help his mother inside.
The truck, as tested, is a $106,000 deal. That is still cheaper than what Ford is asking for the F-150 Raptor R with the 5.2-liter supercharged V8 under the hood, pumping out less power than Ram’s TRX. The 720-horsepower Ford beast starts at $114,420 before options and taxes. That's the good news.
The bad news is that it gets a brutal 12 miles per gallon average, which translates to 19.6 liters per 100 kilometers. Well, anyone driving it knows well before stepping inside that the Ram 1500 SRT TRX is no Toyota Prius in behavior, stance, or fuel economy. To fill an empty tank, he basically becomes a sponsor of the gas station.
Photo: ThatDudeinBlue | YouTube On full load, the supercharger whines from under the hood, making David call it " the loudest factory supercharger I've ever heard in a modern vehicle ." " It’s a symphony to your ears ," he says. The supercharger, along with the HEMI, makes quite an orchestra that he says he hears better with the windows rolled up.
While driving the truck, David has been getting two very distinct reactions from people who either tell him that he is driving the coolest truck I’ve ever seen in my life or roll their eyes at him, as if they have had enough of men driving full-size high-performance trucks to flatter their ego.
David is well aware that the 1500 SRT TRX is not a truck that requires to be pampered. Besides, he is not the kind of owner who keeps his off-roader on the road. His first experience with the TRX was some high-speed driving in the desert, a show-off jump included in the experience.
That sort of off-road behavior confirmed that the TRX is not all show and no go when it leaves the tarmac behind. He had a similar experience in the Ford F-150 Raptor R in the Saudi Arabian desert, and it “absolutely blew me away.”
{fullimg
But above all, he loves how he rides sky-high in the TRX with high ground clearance and massive 35-inch tires. " I feel I should be holding an American flag out the window with the Blue Angels escorting me ." That is the feeling this high-performance truck gives him while driving.
Given the truck’s $106,000 price tag, owners are right to expect a premium ambiance on board the truck. The TRX that David is testing comes with seats in black leather and contrasting red stitching, along with carbon fiber accents on most touchpoints.
He is content with the 14.5-inch vertical touchscreen, which controls most of the functions of the vehicle. In the meantime, the 12.3-inch digital instrument cluster provides all the relevant driving data. Besides He's got all the driving modes at the tap of a finger.
Accessing the surround-view camera is not that fast, as he has to browse through the menu rather than just hit a button on the dashboard. Furthermore, he says the digital rearview camera can be hit by severe lens glare under direct sunlight. And that rounds up the list of complaints.

BMW’s 2028 X7 Shows Realistic Evolutionary Design in New Digital Illustrations
6 photos
Photo: Kolesa
The current BMW X7 is officially going away, and it was about time, because it will soon blow eight candles off its birthday cake, and that’s a bit long in today’s new car game.
Production started back in late 2018, and some four years later, the facelifted iteration came out, featuring the usual updates at the front and rear, as well as some modifications on the inside, and beneath the skin. The model is based on the CLAR (Linie Grosse) platform, which is also shared with the old X5, the previous 7 Series, the discontinued 8 Series, and the XM, among others, and guess what? An updated version of the same construction is the foundation stone of its successor.
The all-new second-generation looks more like another mid-cycle refresh, and that is definitely a compliment for modern-day Bimmers. That’s because most of them have gone down the Neue Klasse route. But not the upcoming BMW X7 , as you already know from the numerous encounters with all kinds of prototypes, joined by the occasional digital illustrations. And this time, it is another case of the latter, because the vehicle depicted in the gallery above is nothing more than a rendered model.
Signed by Kolesa’s Nikita Chuyko and shared online recently, it provides a very realistic look at the all-new BMW X7. The CGIs in question appear to have been inspired by the latest scooped prototype, which was in the M60 xDrive configuration. This model will replace the current X7 M60i, which has a twin-turbocharged 4.4-liter V8 engine with mild-hybrid assistance.
Photo: Kolesa The lump is officially rated at 523 horsepower (530 ps/390 kW) and 553 pound-feet (750 Nm) of torque. The peak output is available at 5,500-6,000 rpm, and the maximum thrust between 1,800 and 4,600 rpm. An eight-speed automatic transmission channels everything to the xDrive all-wheel drive system. From 0 to 60 mph (0-97 kph), this model needs 4.5 seconds, and the top speed is electronically limited to 155 mph (250 kph).
Reports indicate that the upcoming BMW X7 M60 xDrive will likely retain its twin-turbocharged V8 engine, though it should likely have more power. And it is possible that the mill will continue to feature mild-hybrid assistance, rather than going hybrid or plug-in hybrid. Details surrounding the output and thrust are unknown, as you can imagine, but more power is likely, as mentioned above, though don’t expect anything major due to the new emission regulations (Euro 7) on the other side of the Atlantic Ocean.
By the way, you shouldn’t hold your breath for a full-blown M version of the second-generation X7, because it obviously will not happen. Instead, the above-mentioned X7 M60 xDrive will sit at the top of the family until the Alpina version (or is that versions?) arrives.
In terms of design, the all-new BMW X7 will look like an evolution of its predecessor, as we already told you, and these renderings reveal what lies beneath the camouflage. The split lighting units at the front will still be a thing, albeit with vertical instead of horizontal main clusters, and wider and slimmer daytime running lights. The kidney grille will be a bit taller, and will feature horizontal instead of vertical slats.
Photo: Kolesa The lower air intake in the bumper is wider and shorter than before, and the hood hasn’t gone down the clamshell-like path. Just like the smaller X5, the upcoming X7 will feature winglets instead of traditional door handles, and chances are it won’t sport a split-opening tailgate anymore. The taillights are shorter and much wider than before, and the tailgate now blends in with the rear bumper.
The quad tailpipes shown here are an indicator that we are looking at the M60 xDrive version of the flagship crossover, and the wheels have been virtually sourced directly from the scooped tester. Rumor has it that this model might be available with yellow daytime running lights, and it is up to you to decide whether these fit the large and family-friendly nature of this vehicle.
While the exterior will be evolutionary, the cabin will be revolutionary. Well, revolutionary in comparison with the outgoing BMW X7, because there are several other new Bimmers that feature the same layout, including the i3, 3 Series, iX3, X5, and so on. Thus, whether you like it or not, expect the same Panoramic iDrive display, infotainment system, and probably the same quirky steering wheel, among others.
BMW has yet to announce when it will unveil the all-new X7 , but the model could come out of hiding a few months from now. Word on the street is that it could arrive at dealers in the United States of America for the 2028 model year, which makes a lot of sense given that the outgoing one is a 2027 model. Do you fancy the upcoming X7 more than the outgoing one based on these realistic CGIs ?
